description: Machine-readable index tracing every Stage 11 finding to its experiment ID, command, config, seed(s), engine, and artifact. Regenerate any row with the listed command against the listed git commit.

programs.name: Policy Regime Map
programs.key_finding: RR ties exactly under homogeneous load; EWMA wins 18/27 heterogeneous configs on mean latency via unconstrained load concentration (no queueing penalty in the virtual model); Adaptive wins 0/27 on this metric.

programs.name: Adversarial Adaptive Testing
programs.key_finding: B1: Adaptive's cache-affinity signal causes a 0%-post-recovery-return lock-in, confirmed causally by zeroing the weight (restores to 54%). B2: correlated failure did NOT make Adaptive lose (negative result, reported honestly).

programs.name: Recovery and Adaptation Dynamics
programs.key_finding: transition_p99 == steady_state_p99 for every policy (no-queueing model can't express adaptation cost via percentiles); per-phase means show real dynamics, including a signal-scarcity convergence when only one target is available, reproducing Program B's B2 mechanism independently.

programs.name: Distribution Shift
programs.key_finding: Adaptive's disadvantage behind the best policy narrowed under a 5-factor genuine distribution shift (34.8% -> 27.1%), traced to EWMA's own concentration advantage eroding under flash-crowd + mid-run-failure dynamics.

programs.name: Mechanistic Attribution
programs.key_finding: Independently-measured L (event-timeline integration) matches Lambda*W to ~0 relative error for all 6 target/policy pairs -- confirms attribution bookkeeping consistency, explicitly NOT evidence of real queueing dynamics (the model has none).

programs.name: Virtual vs Real Validation
programs.key_finding: Discovered and fixed a real defect: RealEngine discarded policy.New's Instrumentation, so dynamic policies (least-connections/ewma/p2c-load/adaptive) selected blind for the whole run in the real engine. Fixed the latency signal via existing ExposeDebugHeaders infra. Post-fix, EWMA's real behavior closely matches virtual (H4 confirmed for EWMA); Adaptive's ranking direction agrees but concentration diverges (load signal still unfixed).

programs.name: Seed and Reproducibility Attack
programs.root_seeds: 5001 (G1 repeat-run), {Global:0,Traffic:100,Topology:200,Failure:300,Policy:400} baseline +/- one axis at a time (G2, G3)
programs.key_finding: G1: 3x identical repeat runs byte-identical. G2: discovered Topology seed leaks into Failure selection under internal/tuning.DefaultScenarioSpace.Generate (target-count-dependent RNG range), a previously-untested invariant. G3: Policy-seed isolation confirmed, policy-dependent (only p2c-load consumes it).

programs.name: Statistical Robustness Check
programs.key_finding: EWMA beats Adaptive in 12/12 seeds on the flagship severe/constant/none scenario; Cliff's Delta=1.000 (large); bootstrap 95% CI on the mean difference [10.55, 10.89]ms, excludes zero. Not single-run noise.

programs.name: Stage 8 Tuned-Config Reconciliation (ad hoc verification, not a standalone command)
programs.command: see docs/StageArtifacts/Stage11.md Section 19 for the exact AdaptiveConfig used
programs.artifact: no separate JSON artifact -- numbers quoted directly in Stage11.md #19
programs.key_finding: Stage 8's tuned AdaptiveConfig narrows but does not close the gap to EWMA (27.38ms default -> 22.45ms tuned -> still worse than EWMA's 15.90ms) on this scenario -- resolves the apparent tension with Stage 8's 62.5-70% win rate as a metric/scenario-distribution difference, not a contradiction.
